spec.title: codkit PROP-013: How codkit itself is tested

status.comment: standalone Codkit test contract and explicit evidence matrix

facts.TP-REAL-GIT-FAKE-HEAVY: The git operations in the tests are real (real mini repositories); the heavy parts (the VS Code build, the daemons) are emulated by stub scripts.
facts.TP-UNRELATED-PATHS: The toolRoot of the launcher under test, the temporary patchesDir and the temporary forkDir sit at three unrelated absolute paths. Positive cases forbid any assumption about cwd or neighbourhood; negative cases check equality, nesting in both directions and a symlink-prefix bypass of the disjoint-root guard.
facts.TP-OTHER-UID: Where the OS and the CI allow it, the fixture tree is created under another owner and permissions (in a container: chown + a run under another uid) to check `safe.directory` and the permissions.
facts.TP-POISON-GITCONFIG: Every unit test is isolated from the git configuration of the machine (the `gitx` wrapper); a separate test checks that a «poisoned» global configuration — `core.autocrlf=true`, `diff.algorithm=histogram`, hooks, templates — does not affect the result.
facts.TP-RUNNER: The runner is vitest (`common/PROP-000` `##CODKIT-TEST-RUNNER-VITEST`); the tests live in `packages/codkit/test/{unit,e2e}/`; on flakes: the tests that depend on timings (buildWrap) use controlled stubs, not real sleeps.
facts.TP-NO-MUTATION-TESTING: Mutation testing is NOT used (an owner decision of 2026-08-31, to save budget): the quality is held by exact detailed assignments written from the specs, by the coverage of the error codes (§8) and by the e2e scenarios of FEAT-002. To be revisited at the first incident of «a green test let a defect through of a class that mutation would have caught».

p.FIXTURE-UPSTREAM: **The pseudo-upstream (a «mini VS Code»)** is generated by code (`packages/codkit/test/fixtures/makeUpstream.ts`): a git repository of ~40 files that repeats the **shape** of VS Code which matters to codkit: `src/vs/workbench/**` with 2–3 TS files (including a file with a `constructor(` and a `create*` method), a CSS file, `product.json`, a `package.json` with the stub scripts `watch-client-transpile` and others (the scripts print the verbatim pass-boundary markers from `toolRoot/config/build-watch.json` and sleep), `resources/` with a binary, `.nvmrc`. The history: the root commit (the anchor) → the tag `t1` (the «old pin») → the changes: an edit of the target file, a **rename** of one file (an analogue of R096), a deletion of one file, an edit of a constructor (a future conflict) → the tag `t2` (the «new pin»). LFS is not emulated (the lfs check uses a separate mock of `git lfs version`).

p.FIXTURE-PATCHSET: **The pseudo patch set** is generated by `makePatchSet.ts`: `codkit.json`, `delta/` with samples of the layers, the cycle and runtime directories and a short Git history. It deliberately holds no sources, launchers, package manifest or safety defaults of Codkit.

unit.title: 3. Unit tests (by the modules of PROP-002 §3)

tr.td: Module
Key cases

toolRoot only from the install; for patches/fork the three sources flag/env/settings and an independent precedence; CLI/env relative to cwd, settings absolute-only; an empty selected source rejects; a missing one is null; canonicalization and all overlap/nesting cases; source/exists output
all comment forms; nesting/unpaired/duplicate id/broken id; CRLF; non-UTF-8; the benchmark «fractions of a second per file»
reading and writing of the header; a refusal on an unknown version; the encoding of names (`__`, a collision); add-file; the ban on delete-file
the LF/CRLF/EOF-newline predicates; trailing whitespace is preserved; an empty diff is not written; byte stability on a repeat; a binary file is a refusal

without `--layer` the stub always contains `layer:"patch"`; `--layer entry-module` passes into pending and then into the `# layer:` of the new patch; `rewrite-rule` and an unknown value are rejected; an existing header is not rewritten
additions outside the block; «neutralization by commenting out» is admissible; deleting an upstream line without a copy is an error
set/remove; `$var`; `expectUpstream` (matched / diverged / `$absent`); serialization with tabs
completeness against the diff (`UNTRACKED-INTERVENTION`, `STALE-ARTIFACT`); the inventory diff; determinism of the serialization
the comparison rule of PROP-006 §1: each of the 6 conditions is broken separately → the fast path is forbidden
one test per class clean/shifted/merged/conflict/target-deleted/target-renamed/rule-broken on the t1→t2 fixture
porting of the patch + the test + the import; the similarity threshold; similarity<100 is flagged
a single commit; narrowing with `-L`; a deleted file; `approx`

the precedence `--patch → .orig → HEAD` of an unfinished merge → `HEAD^1` of a finished merge; every earlier source shadows the later ones; `MERGE_HEAD` is never taken as the feature patch; a full refusal lists the sources that were checked

an explicit ref and the fixed default `refs/remotes/upstream/main` are resolved once into a full SHA; a fresher `origin/main` has no effect; `--ci` without `--ref` is rejected before the tree is accessed; an unreachable ref gives a deterministic hint without a fetch

exactly two parents (`HEAD^1` feature, `HEAD^2` target); refusals for non-merge/octopus/swapped roles; the set of patches comes from `merge-base..HEAD^1`, and a target-only patch is not ported; the scratch base equals the applied `HEAD^2`; `pin` is updated to the target, `cause` is preserved for clean and updated for shifted/merged/conflict; a conflicting pending does not write a new header with the old body

for CI/publish the commit order `patch → own → overlay → resource`, with a deterministic sort inside a layer and empty layers skipped; a local load skips the own slot, copies own after the checkout and does not make it tracked
contention between two processes; a stale lock from a dead pid
parsing of logs with ANSI; false ends (`falseEndGuards`); the counter flag vs the real number of errors; the timeout

a clean fixture → 0 problems; one defect of S29 (a)–(s) at a time → exactly one problem with the expected code and path; the window of 20 non-empty lines; the carrier block ends with the SPDX line; a sidecar replaces the scan; the `REUSE.toml` registry and the allowlist; normalization of the quotes and of the whitespace of the UPL text; the policy is read only from toolRoot and a patch-set file does not shadow it

absent → an append with LF normalization; present-equal → the bytes do not change; present-different → a replacement only inside the block; malformed (a single marker, a repeat, the order) → a refusal without a write; an entry about the package outside the block → a refusal with the line number; CR → a CRLF refusal; a tail after the block → a warning

exactly one `v*` in toolRoot, and the version equals `[package] version`; comparison of the trees: identical / modified / extra / missing / symlink; the scratch `.codkit-load-*` is removed and printed; a rename onto an existing target → a repeated classification

the shipped package passes `licenseCheck` with zero problems; `LICENSES/UPL-1.0.txt` is byte-for-byte equal to the constant of `licenseTexts.ts`; `LICENSE` without the header lines equals the canonical text without the placeholder

exactly one version directory; the version literal equals the name of the directory; `.ts`/`.md` only; the four header lines in every file; `checkLicenseCarriers` → 0 problems; the imports follow `RT-NARROW-UPSTREAM-SURFACE`; no product names; no non-ASCII outside the header comments (PROP-015 §3)

0/1/2 version directories and a mismatched literal → `RUNTIME-PACKAGE`; the plan for absent/identical/drift; `--upgrade` replaces the whole of it; a dry run writes nothing; the notice with the components block in both roots; a stale copy is deleted

`isDeliveredByCodkit` for the notice and for `codkit/**`; the unit coverage skips what was delivered; `OWN-UNDER-CODKIT`, `RUNTIME-DRIFT`, `HOOK-TOO-LARGE` — a separate test for each error; `save` refuses with `DELIVERED-EDIT`; the synthetic inventory entry

an annotation covers a file that has no comment style; a source carrying only an annotation — `LICENSE-HEADER`; a nested `REUSE.toml`, where the deeper one wins; an own annotation with a foreign copyright holder is an error; a differential test against the reference on 25 fixtures (a–x)
the shape of an id; the three files; the product header from the flags, or a warning when there is no header; `GEN-EXISTS` without a write; `gen brand`
the PROP-012 §1 envelope; human output goes to stderr under `--json`

p.E2E-HARNESS: The harness runs the CLI from a real toolRoot as a subprocess and creates patchesDir/forkDir separately. It checks the schema-2 `roots`, a settings-only invocation from an unrelated cwd and the mini versions of S01–S19 (including the fork-tree commits: S17a/b/c, S18, S19 in `treeCommits.test.ts` — the replay by commits, idempotency through the `replayCheckpoint` test seam, a refusal on an intermediate state outside a marker; the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign). Full VS Code scenarios are a separate integration baseline and are not substituted by mini fixtures.

p.E2E-REBASE-SURFACE: The rebase fixture builds feature and target from a common merge base, changes different artifacts on both sides, merges target into feature with the required order of parents and checks: the sources come from `HEAD^1`, the target baseline from `HEAD^2`, a target-only artifact is not classified as feature, clean/shifted/merged are regenerated onto the target pin, and a conflict keeps the full list and after `save` receives the target `pin/cause` atomically.

p.E2E-PUBLISH-SURFACE: The publish fixture uses a local bare remote and a full set of patch/own/overlay/resource. Both signatures of the profile are checked (the heavy steps are fixture stubs), the mandatory bot flag, the refusal to combine it with `--ci`, an unsuccessful `ls-remote` leaving the tree and the refs unchanged, the exact order of the generated commits, the exact trailers `Codkit-Patchset-Commit`/`Codkit-Upstream-Pin`, a branch with exactly 12 hex characters, and force-with-lease for the branch only. For the local test contract `--release 1.2.3` creates `patchset-v1.2.3+<pin.tag>`: a repeat on the same tip is a no-op, and an attempt with the same tag on another tip is a refusal without force; the test does not pre-empt the external owner decision about the final naming.

p.E2E-STANDARDS-SURFACE: The standards fixture is a patchesDir with a written `vibe.toml` `[project]` and without a forkDir; the e2e `licenseCheck.test.ts` and `standards.test.ts` play S29–S34 through the real launcher; the `vibe install --offline` step runs only when `vibe` is on PATH and is otherwise skipped with an explicit mark, because vibe is not a dependency of codkit; the `CODKIT_TEST_STANDARDS_SOURCE` seam is in force only under `--conditions=codkit-test`.

p.E2E-RUNTIME-SURFACE: The runtime fixture is a patchesDir with `codkit.json` and `delta/own/` without a forkDir; the e2e `runtime.test.ts` plays S42–S48 through the real launcher (creation, idempotency, a refusal on drift without a write, `--upgrade`, `check`, a `save` refusal on an edit of a delivered file, `verify` on a unit under `codkit/`); `gen.test.ts` — S49–S50; the notice and `standards license` — S51 in `standards.test.ts`; the `CODKIT_TEST_RUNTIME_SOURCE` seam is in force only under `--conditions=codkit-test`.

p.RESUMABILITY-TESTS: On the t1→t2 fixture: the cycle is run with an injected crash (the env `CODKIT_TEST_CRASH_AT=<phase>`, supported only in the test build) after each phase of PROP-009 §4: init, apply (before and after the state is written), resolve, deps-advisory, stabilize. After every crash a new `cycle continue` process must carry the cycle through to `done` without losing data; `cycle status` reflects the actual state at any point. Separately: `restart` returns the branch to the parent of the pin commit and removes the state.

p.SYNC-CRASH-TESTS: The crash atoms of the two-way `codkit sync` (the TREE-COMMITS-SAVE campaign, Phase 8+8b, decisions D20/D21; the e2e `syncTwoWay.test.ts` and `syncConflict.test.ts`): the env `CODKIT_TEST_SYNC_CRASH_AT=<atom>` (the test build only, a hard exit 86 in the style of `CODKIT_TEST_SAVE_REPLAY_CRASH_AT`) at every atom that has a seam — `transaction-written` (before the first mutation), `conflict-materialized` (after every written pair of markers, Phase 8b), `state-committed` (after every patch-set commit), `worktree-moved`, `mark-written` (the two post-checkout rebuild windows). After every crash three facts are proved, not a single exit code: the file `.codkit/sync-transaction.json` exists and contains the atoms that were written (`patchsetCommits` according to the stage); a new process running `load` or `save` refuses with `CK-E-SYNC-IN-PROGRESS` (exit 1); `status` prints `sync in progress: <id>, conflicts: N`. Phase 8b added the recovery matrix (`syncConflict.test.ts`): after a crash at every atom both roads — `--continue` and `--abort` — lead to a definite state (a continuation finishes the run or refuses naming the file: the markers are not resolved / the merge did not reach the file), and `--abort` restores the bytes, HEAD and the branches against the sha256 snapshots taken before the run over deliberately distinguishable bytes. A separate red run (the inversion «the transaction before the refusal») holds the main invariant of S25: a refusal of both sides leaves neither a record file, nor a moved ref, nor a changed byte.

facts.DET-LINUX-CURRENT: The current automated floor and the standalone disjoint-root e2e were executed on Linux.
facts.DET-NATIVE-MATRIX: The native macOS/Windows matrix stays an acceptance gate: unit + e2e + the Bash/PowerShell launcher + S16 + Git and path semantics. Emulation or a platform-neutral review does not close the row.
facts.DET-WINDOWS: The Windows row includes paths with spaces and Unicode, the longpaths warning, the CRLF guard, PowerShell argv/exit propagation and the process-tree lifecycle.
facts.DET-AIRGAP: The air-gapped test: an e2e run with `netAllowed=false` and a mock that fails on any networked git command, including `ls-remote`; plus, on the polygon, `docker run --network none` (S14; the method: a container without a network — any attempt to connect gives an error, and the test checks that there are no network errors in the output). A separate publish test proves that the network is enabled only with the bot flag, that `--ci` is not used, and that `ls-remote` precedes the first mutation.

double-regen.title: 7. The test «a double regeneration gives an empty diff» (normative)

p.DOUBLE-REGEN-STEPS: The steps: fixture → `load` → a deterministic edit → `save` → a snapshot of the patch bytes → a return → the same edit → `save` → an empty `git diff -- delta/` and an unchanged mtime on the untouched artifacts. Linux runs this in the current PR floor; macOS and Windows run the same test natively before cross-platform acceptance is declared.

facts.COVERAGE-ERROR-CODES: Every error code of the registry of PROP-012 §2 is covered by at least one test that triggers it.
facts.TASK-DONE-WITH-TESTS: Every change of behavior is closed together with a unit or e2e proof of the corresponding addressable contract; an external execution plan is not the source of this norm.
